children.name: Lightning is a natural electrical phenomenon produced by the accumulation and sudden discharge of electric charges inside clouds or between clouds and the Earth. It is one of the largest natural examples of static electricity.

children.name: Normally, air acts as an insulator and prevents the movement of charges. However, when the amount of charge becomes extremely large, the potential difference between oppositely charged regions increases enormously. At this stage, the insulating property of air breaks down. The air becomes ionised and suddenly allows electric current to pass through it.

children.name: Conductors are materials that allow electric charges to flow through them easily (e.g., copper, aluminium). Insulators are materials that do not allow electric charges to pass through them (e.g., wood, plastic). Conductors are used for making wires, while insulators are used for covering wires to prevent shocks.

children.name: Lightning is a huge electric spark caused by the sudden discharge of a large amount of electric charge accumulated in the clouds. children.name: An electric fuse contains a thin wire of low melting point. When current exceeds the safe limit, the wire gets heated, melts, and breaks the circuit. This stops the flow of excess current and protects the appliance and wiring from damage. It is called a safety device because it prevents fire and damage due to overloading or short circuit.

children.name: When the switch is pressed, current flows through the coil and the electromagnet attracts the soft iron strip. The hammer strikes the gong and produces sound. At the same time, the strip loses contact with the screw, breaking the circuit. The electromagnet loses its magnetism and the strip returns to its original position due to the spring. This again completes the circuit. The process repeats rapidly, so the bell keeps ringing continuously as long as the switch is pressed.

children.name: In power plants, electricity is generated by converting mechanical energy into electrical energy using an electric generator.
